minutes.headline: Commission approved a Horizon Island Road rebuild and a trails grant bid; Reservoir Road remediation stays open to March 6.
minutes.summary: The commission approved a house demolition and rebuild with a 30-foot waiver and gave a negative determination for five shed lots. Most of the meeting was a workshop with residents on riverfront overages at 155 Reservoir Road, set to return March 6. It also debated the Lake Shirley drawdown and voted to pursue a state trails grant.

public_comment.topic: Chair opened public comment; none offered.
Described the riverfront area, ten percent limit and current disturbance at Reservoir Road.
Opposed opening dam gates or changing the lake level under ice for safety; supported DEP stopping the drawdown.
Agreed on safety and asked whether the Commission or DEP is the higher authority.

what_happened.line: The commission approved an order of conditions for a house demolition and rebuild at 98 Horizon Island Road, with a waiver for work in the 30-foot no-touch zone.
The commission voted to let the agent pursue a state trails grant through the town manager; the required match can be in kind.
A long workshop on riverfront overages at 155 Reservoir Road ended with the matter set to return March 6 after the engineer and residents draft plans.
The 55 Spring Street applicant was told to file a new RDA, to be heard February 6.
The Lake Shirley drawdown was debated without resolution; a draft order of conditions is to be on the February 20 agenda.

why_it_matters: The Reservoir Road case and the Lake Shirley drawdown decide what riverfront and lakeshore owners may do on their land and who sets the lake level under ice.
The trails grant could pay for signs, markers and gates, and the match could draw on the timber rights fund, so town money may be involved.
